title: Linked lists
hook: A linked list doesn’t jump by index — it walks node to node. That’s the trade.

steps.caption: Start at the head. Each node only knows the next one.

nodeCaptions.head: The head is just a pointer to the first node.
nodeCaptions.n1: Payload + pointer to the next node. No “slot 2” math.

steps.caption: To reach C you must walk A → B → C. No skipping.

nodeCaptions.n2: Inserting after a node is easy: rewire one pointer.
nodeCaptions.n3: Finding the k-th item costs k steps — that’s the downside.

takeaways: Linked lists trade random access for cheap inserts/deletes at a known node.
You follow pointers; you don’t compute addresses from an index.
Poor cache locality is why lists often lose to arrays in practice.

quiz.question: What’s the cost of reaching the 50th node in a singly linked list?
choices: Always one jump, like an array
About 50 pointer hops from the head
It lives at a fixed disk sector
